resources.string: Collect highlights from Kindle\'s notebook screen
Reads highlight text on Kindle\'s notebook screen only, for bulk import. Reads nothing from any other app.
Automatic scrolling failed. Scroll to the end yourself, then tap Done
No highlights read. Make sure you are on the notebook screen, or scroll once.
Appends to the end of the file. The built-in URI cannot target a section.
Appends to the end of the file
No books yet. Add one so the source line and {title} can be filled in.
Share from another app, or select text there and Copy, then read it in here. Apps whose share sheet has a length limit (Kindle, for one) are more reliable this way, and the text comes out cleaner.
Tap a heading to fold it
Default path for a new destination
Where it goes, which section, and in what format. A path may contain {title} {author} {year}, filled from the chosen book — so one "book notes" destination serves every book.
Long-press to drag. Same order as the write screen.
What you are reading — title, author and year, and nothing about where it goes.
Can target a section. Needs the Advanced URI plugin.
No plugin needed, but it can only append to the end of a file.
Off: Obsidian opens the note it just wrote and stays there. On: you go straight back to where you shared from.
Read the clipboard when the app opens
Replaces what is on screen when opened from the launcher or the tile; entering by sharing is unaffected.
Normalise line endings and invisible characters
Drop lines that are only a URL
Used when a share\'s source is not recognised.
Failed sends go to a queue. They are only retried while this app is open — Android will not let a background task start Obsidian.

To get around Kindle\'s share and copy limits: it forbids selecting a long passage in the reading view, so sharing one and copying one both fail. The notebook screen puts each highlight in the accessibility tree as plain text, so reading it works — no selection, no clipboard.
Experimental: the heuristics read screen structure, so a Kindle redesign may break them. That is why anything collected is shown for review before it is written.
The last collection is still waiting to be checked.
Ready. Open this book\'s notebook page in Kindle, then tap the button — it reads the whole list by itself.
System settings show it as enabled, but the service is not actually running (seen on Xiaomi). Toggling that switch off and back on fixes it.

The service is not on yet. Settings → Accessibility → "Downloaded services" → find "Collect highlights from Kindle\'s notebook screen" → turn it on and tap Allow in the dialog. Note this is not the "Accessibility shortcut" toggle at the top of that page, which is for a shortcut button.
Write collected highlights straight away, without review

Off by default. Kindle collapses long highlights, and a collapsed one looks exactly like a short one — with this on they are written unreviewed, while collapsed and already-written ones are still held back for you.
